children: US Treasury yields briefly extended their move higher on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady, as expected, with policymakers choosing to delay changes to borrowing costs before the November US midterm elections.
In a 10-2 decision, the US central bank said it would maintain its benchmark interest rate within the current 3.75%-4.00%. The Fed also was awaiting further data on the path of inflation.
The Fed hiked rates in September for the first time in about three years.
The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note
was last up 4.3 basis points at 5.036%. The yield on the 30-year bond (US30YT=RR) was up 2.9 bps at 5.334%.
The two-year (US2YT=RR) US Treasury yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Fed, was up 4 bps at 4.777%.
No move before midterm elections in November
